Topics · Death and what comes after

Is dying like falling asleep?

The Quran joins sleep and death, each morning a small return. No complete answer is known of the in-between.

Part 1 of 4

﴿ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلْأَنفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِهَا وَٱلَّتِى لَمْ تَمُتْ فِى مَنَامِهَا ۖ فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِى قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَـَٔايَـٰتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Allāh takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that do not die [He takes] during their sleep. Then He keeps those for which He has decreed death and releases the others for a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:42

Translation

If he set his heart on himself, if he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath, all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.

Original · Hebrew

אִם־יָשִׂ֣ים אֵלָ֣יו לִבּ֑וֹ רוּח֥וֹ וְ֝נִשְׁמָת֗וֹ אֵלָ֥יו יֶאֱסֹֽף׃ יִגְוַ֣ע כָּל־בָּשָׂ֣ר יָ֑חַד וְ֝אָדָ֗ם עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָשֽׁוּב׃

Job · 34:14-15

World English Bible

Every night you go somewhere you cannot report on, and every morning you come back, sometimes remembering nothing of the gap. The verse puts sleep and death under one description: God takes souls at death, and takes the souls of sleepers too. He keeps those on whom death is decreed, and sends back the others until an appointed time. So the Quran gives your question a picture, not a proof: a likeness, not a full description.

A question for you

What do you remember of deep sleep?

If you sayNothing at all
ThenAnd yet you came back. That is what the verse points to: the gap with no memory has been crossed many times by everyone reading this.
If you sayA sense of rest
ThenRest is a name the Quran gives sleep in another verse. It is among the gentlest likenesses for death, without being a description of it.
If you sayOnly waking
ThenThat fits sleep: no sleeper witnesses the crossing. What we witness is the return.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يَتَوَفَّىٰكُم بِٱلَّيْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُم بِٱلنَّهَارِ ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ لِيُقْضَىٰٓ أَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى ۖ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ مَرْجِعُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And it is He who takes your souls by night[312] and knows what you have committed by day. Then He revives you therein [i.e., by day] that a specified term[313] may be fulfilled. Then to Him will be your return; then He will inform you about what you used to do.

Translator's notes

[312] i.e., when you sleep. [313] One's decreed life span.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:60

Translation

I cry to Yahweh with my voice, and he answers me out of his holy hill. Selah. I laid myself down and slept. I awakened, for Yahweh sustains me.

Original · Hebrew

ק֭וֹלִי אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֶקְרָ֑א וַיַּֽעֲנֵ֨נִי מֵהַ֖ר קָדְשׁ֣וֹ סֶֽלָה׃ אֲנִ֥י שָׁכַ֗בְתִּי וָֽאִ֫ישָׁ֥נָה הֱקִיצ֑וֹתִי כִּ֖י יְהוָ֣ה יִסְמְכֵֽנִי׃

the Psalms · 3:4-5

World English Bible

The verse makes each day lie between two small returns: evening takes you, morning sends you back to complete an appointed term. It adds that the one who knows what you did by day is the one who raises you in the day. Then in the end you go back to Him. This verse describes no pain, and no detail of what follows death. It describes a return: the one who takes you at night is the one who gives you back in the morning, and knows your day.

A question for you

When you wake, do you feel you have been given your day back, or that you simply resume it?

If you sayGiven back
ThenThat is close to the verse's language: raises you in it. A return is a gift, not an entitlement.
If you sayI simply resume
ThenThat is how most of us wake, because the return happens without notice. The verse invites noticing what has always been happening.
If you sayI do not know
ThenAn honest answer. Try tomorrow to notice, then tell yourself what you saw.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَٱلنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ نُشُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And it is He who has made the night for you as clothing[1030] and sleep [a means for] rest and has made the day a resurrection.[1031]

Translator's notes

[1030] Covering you in darkness and providing rest. [1031] For renewal of life and activity.

Quran · Al-Furqan 25:47

Translation

In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you alone, Yahweh, make me live in safety.

Original · Hebrew

בְּשָׁל֣וֹם יַחְדָּו֮ אֶשְׁכְּבָ֪ה וְאִ֫ישָׁ֥ן כִּֽי־אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה לְבָדָ֑ד לָ֝בֶ֗טַח תּוֹשִׁיבֵֽנִי׃

the Psalms · 4:8

World English Bible

The verse gives this state gentle names: night a garment, sleep a rest and a pause, day a rising up. It is worth noticing that the word for rising is the one the Quran uses elsewhere for rising after death. So it names what resembles death a rest, and names the return by the same word it uses for the great return. There is some reassurance in that.

A question for you

Which of these is closer to your picture of death?

If you sayA rest
ThenThe verse calls sleep a rest, and says nothing more of the dead. No complete description of what lies between death and rising is known, and Muslims differ on how to read the little that is said.
If you sayA passing on into another form
ThenThat is the teaching of many traditions, Buddhism and Hinduism among them. What these verses share with them is the sense that a life does not simply stop. The Quran speaks of a return to God.
If you sayAn ending
ThenThe verses answer with a likeness, not an argument: each night ends and is given back. That answer imposes nothing on you. It sets before you what you already know.
If you sayI do not know
ThenAn honest position, and there is some truth in it: no complete knowledge is to be had here.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَكَذَٰلِكَ بَعَثْنَـٰهُمْ لِيَتَسَآءَلُوا۟ بَيْنَهُمْ ۚ قَالَ قَآئِلٌ مِّنْهُمْ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ ۖ قَالُوا۟ لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ ۚ قَالُوا۟ رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثْتُمْ فَٱبْعَثُوٓا۟ أَحَدَكُم بِوَرِقِكُمْ هَـٰذِهِۦٓ إِلَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ فَلْيَنظُرْ أَيُّهَآ أَزْكَىٰ طَعَامًا فَلْيَأْتِكُم بِرِزْقٍ مِّنْهُ وَلْيَتَلَطَّفْ وَلَا يُشْعِرَنَّ بِكُمْ أَحَدًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And similarly,[782] We awakened them that they might question one another. Said a speaker from among them, "How long have you remained [here]?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord is most knowing of how long you remained. So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city and let him look to which is the best of food and bring you provision from it and let him be cautious. And let no one be aware of you.

Translator's notes

[782] By the will of Allāh.

Quran · Al-Kahf 18:19

A story of people who slept a very long time and woke. One asked: how long have you stayed? They answered: a day or part of a day. This is a report of how it felt to those who crossed the gap: they did not feel the long time. The verse does not say the dead are sleeping. It is a story of sleepers. But it gives another meaning: a return may feel like waking, not like a long journey.

A question for you

If you crossed a long gap without feeling it, what would matter once you woke?

If you sayWhere I am now
ThenThat is what the people in the story do: they question one another, then act. The present is what asks for attention.
If you sayWho is with me
ThenIn the story they are companions who wake together and ask together. The first thing they do on waking is turn to one another.
If you sayHow long it has been
ThenTheir answer is that they do not know, and that knowledge is with God. There is reassurance in that: you do not have to count.

The same in the other books

Translation

It is vain for you to rise up early, to stay up late, eating the bread of toil, for he gives sleep to his loved ones.

Original · Hebrew

שָׁ֤וְא לָכֶ֨ם ׀ מַשְׁכִּ֪ימֵי ק֡וּם מְאַֽחֲרֵי־שֶׁ֗בֶת אֹ֭כְלֵי לֶ֣חֶם הָעֲצָבִ֑ים כֵּ֤ן יִתֵּ֖ן לִֽידִיד֣וֹ שֵׁנָֽא׃

the Psalms · 127:2

World English Bible

Your reflection

When you think of death, what is the first feeling that comes? Does that feeling have a name you like?
